incotermsGuide.title: Delivery terms explained
incotermsGuide.subtitle: Incoterms® 2020 — who arranges shipping, insurance and customs, and where risk passes. Here, Seller means you.

EXW.summary: You just make the goods ready at your site. The buyer arranges pickup, export, shipping and everything after — the simplest, cheapest option for you.

FCA.summary: You hand the goods, cleared for export, to the carrier the buyer chose. The buyer pays the main shipping and insurance.

FOB.summary: For sea freight: you load the goods onto the ship and clear export. From there the buyer pays sea freight and insurance.

CFR.summary: For sea freight: you pay the freight to the destination port, but the buyer's risk starts once the goods are on the ship.

CIF.summary: Like CFR, but you also buy basic cargo insurance up to the destination port. Common for sea shipments.

CPT.summary: You pay transport to the agreed destination, but the buyer's risk starts as soon as the first carrier takes the goods.

CIP.summary: Like CPT, and you also insure the cargo up to the destination. Works for any transport mode.

DAP.summary: You deliver all the way to the destination, ready for the buyer to unload. The buyer only handles import customs.

DPU.summary: You deliver to the destination and unload the goods there. The buyer handles import customs.

DDP.summary: You deliver to the buyer's door with import duties paid — the most you can take on, and the easiest for the buyer.
